articles.title: Proximal Ventures: $27.5 Million Debut Fund To Back AI-Native Life Sciences Companies
articles.snippet:
Proximal Ventures, a San Francisco-based early-stage venture capital firm focused on artificial intelligence and life sciences, has closed its inaugural fund at $27.5 million, exceeding its original $25 million fundraising target. The fund will invest in pre-seed and seed-stage companies developing AI-native software and infrastructure across pharmaceutical research, clinical development, manufacturing, and commercialization.
The post Proximal Ventures: $27.5 Million Debut Fund To Back AI-Native Life Sciences Companies appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Proximal Ventures: $27.5 Million Debut Fund To Back AI-Native Life Sciences Companies
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:36 AM
Proximal Ventures: $27.5 Million Debut Fund To Back AI-Native Life Sciences Companies
Proximal Ventures, a San Francisco-based early-stage venture capital firm focused on artificial intelligence and life sciences, has closed its inaugural fund at $27.5 million, exceeding its original $25 million fundraising target. The fund will invest in pre-seed and seed-stage companies developing AI-native software and infrastructure across pharmaceutical research, clinical development, manufacturing, and commercialization.
Founded in 2026 by Sahir Raoof, Proximal Ventures is pursuing a specialized investment strategy centered on the pharmaceutical value chain, supporting emerging technologies from molecular discovery through the delivery of medicines to patients.
The fund is backed by strategic partners including Domino Lane, SignalFire, Kleiner Perkins, Bertelsmann Healthcare Investments, and PagsGroup. Individual investors include Nan Li and Zavain Dar, co-founders of venture capital firm Dimension.
Proximal’s investment thesis reflects the growing application of AI across life sciences, where advances in computational research are creating opportunities to improve drug discovery and development.
While much of the industry’s attention has focused on using AI to identify new therapeutic candidates, Proximal sees additional opportunities in the processes required to develop, manufacture, approve, and commercialize medicines.
These activities represent a substantial portion of pharmaceutical industry spending and involve complex regulatory, scientific, and operational requirements.
The firm intends to support startups developing technologies capable of improving efficiency, reducing costs, and accelerating workflows throughout these processes.
Potential investment areas include computational drug discovery, clinical trial infrastructure, pharmaceutical manufacturing systems, and technologies supporting market access and commercialization.
Proximal believes AI-native companies can address operational challenges that have historically received less venture capital attention than drug discovery platforms.
Supporting Founders From Company Formation
Proximal differentiates its investment approach through direct involvement with founders during the earliest stages of company development.
The firm works with entrepreneurs to validate business ideas, develop go-to-market strategies, and establish relationships with prospective pharmaceutical customers.
In some cases, Proximal begins supporting founders before their companies have been formally incorporated.
This approach is intended to help startups develop products based on actual requirements within the pharmaceutical industry.
Life sciences technology companies frequently face challenges involving lengthy sales cycles, regulatory requirements, integration with existing systems, and the need to demonstrate value to specialized customers.
Proximal aims to address these issues by connecting founders with industry executives, technology partners, and potential design customers.
Its advisory network includes Amy Abernethy, Co-Founder of Highlander Health and former Principal Deputy Commissioner of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
The network also includes Kim Branson, Chief AI Officer at GSK, along with other senior executives from pharmaceutical and technology companies.

articles.title: Finite State Raises $27 Million Series C to Expand AI-Powered Device Security
articles.snippet: Finite State Raises $27 Million Series C to Expand AI-Powered Device Security Unite.AI
articles.text:
Funding
Finite State Raises $27 Million Series C to Expand AI-Powered Device Security
Published
November 10, 2026
By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Matt Wyckhouse (Founder & CEO). Photo: Finite State.
Finite State has raised $27 million in Series C funding to expand its AI-driven product security platform and international operations. The round was led by private funds managed by The O.H.I.O. Fund , with participation from CIBC Innovation Banking , Energy Impact Partners , Energize Capital , and National Grid Partners .
The Columbus, Ohio-based company focuses on a problem that becomes more consequential as vulnerability discovery accelerates: manufacturers need to know what software actually runs inside the devices they sell. A flaw in a shared component can affect vehicles, medical equipment, industrial systems, or consumer electronics, but determining which finished products contain that component can be difficult.
Finite State plans to use the capital to deepen its presence in international markets and develop more autonomous platform capabilities. Its technology combines analysis of software artifacts with vulnerability intelligence and compliance workflows, aiming to turn an inventory of shipped code into decisions about what needs attention.
Inspecting the Software That Actually Ships
Connected products are assembled from many sources: an operating system, open-source libraries, supplier SDKs, board-support packages, and proprietary applications. Manufacturers may control their own source code while having limited visibility into compiled components supplied by other vendors.
A build manifest describes what a development process expects to include. Firmware analysis examines the artifact produced by that process. The difference matters when packaging adds a component, a supplier modifies a library, or a dependency is compiled directly into an executable.
Finite State’s binary-analysis documentation describes unpacking firmware images, containers, archives, and executables, then identifying components through binary software composition analysis. It also applies static application security testing to compiled code, examining weaknesses beyond a simple list of package names.
The resulting inventory can include modified and statically linked components, with findings enriched by vulnerability, exploit, and license information. The analysis also looks for hard-coded credentials, exposed keys, and cryptographic issues. Supported inputs include firmware, shared libraries, mobile application binaries, and third-party software, as well as source code when available.
This is the foundation of the company’s pitch: security decisions should follow the contents of the finished product, rather than depend entirely on the documentation that accompanies it.
Turning a Component Inventory Into a Remediation Decision
Finding a vulnerable component is only the beginning. A product team still needs to determine whether the affected code can be reached, whether an exploit is relevant to the device’s configuration, and which releases or product variants need a fix.
Finite State’s platform overview describes prioritization based on reachability, exploit intelligence, and product context. The aim is to reduce the time engineers spend investigating findings that do not represent the same level of practical exposure.

Finite State raises $27 million for device security platform
Finite State has secured $27 million in Series C funding to enhance its AI-driven product security platform. This investment will support global expansion and platform autonomy for connected device manufacturers.
TechGig
Updated On Nov 12, 2026 at 11:40 AM IST
Highlights
Finite State secured $27 million in Series C funding to expand its platform.
The O.H.I.O. Fund led the round with multiple other investors participating.
The platform inspects device software and firmware for vulnerabilities without source code.
It generates SBOMs and VEX documents for compliance with global regulations.
Product security firm Finite State announced on Tuesday that it raised $27 million in a Series C funding round.
The company aims to grow its international presence and make its connected device security platform more autonomous. Private funds managed by The O.H.I.O. Fund led the round, with participation from CIBC Innovation Banking, Energy Impact Partners, Energize Capital, and National Grid Partners.
Advt
The investment addresses two key pressures on manufacturers, according to the company. These include critical flaws like the ‘Vulnpocalypse’ and increasing product security mandates. Finite State’s platform inspects software and firmware in devices, operating from compiled binaries without requiring source code.
It identifies both known and zero-day vulnerabilities, helping manufacturers fix exploitable flaws. On the compliance front, the platform continuously produces SBOMs, VEX documents, and signed compliance packages. This supports device makers in meeting regulations such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), FDA premarket cybersecurity requirements, UNECE R155 and R156 vehicle regulations, and the IEC 62443 industrial standard.

articles.title: University Of Tennessee: $27 Million Army Research Laboratory Renewal To Advance Military Materials And Manufacturing
articles.snippet:
The University of Tennessee has secured up to $27 million in renewed sponsorship from the U.S. Department of War's Army Research Laboratory to advance materials science and manufacturing technologies supporting military applications.
The post University Of Tennessee: $27 Million Army Research Laboratory Renewal To Advance Military Materials And Manufacturing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
University Of Tennessee: $27 Million Army Research Laboratory Renewal To Advance Military Materials And Manufacturing
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 5:34 PM
University Of Tennessee: $27 Million Army Research Laboratory Renewal To Advance Military Materials And Manufacturing
The University of Tennessee has secured up to $27 million in renewed sponsorship from the U.S. Department of War’s Army Research Laboratory to advance materials science and manufacturing technologies supporting military applications.
The funding will support the university’s multidisciplinary Defense Development and Applied Research Center (DARC) and multiple departments within the Tickle College of Engineering from 2026 through 2030.
The research focuses on developing advanced materials, improving manufacturing processes, and addressing supply chain challenges affecting military equipment.
New Partnership With Leidos
The renewed sponsorship will support a new research partnership between the university and industrial partner Leidos.
The collaboration will examine equipment assembly timelines and identify supply chain bottlenecks that could be addressed through additive manufacturing.
Researchers will investigate alternative manufacturing approaches that can produce mission-critical components faster or at lower cost while maintaining or improving performance.
The university’s capabilities include developing carbon-based composites, hybrid materials, and ceramic composites designed to withstand demanding operating environments.
Researchers also use advanced imaging and characterization equipment to evaluate complex materials, including additively manufactured components.
Expanding Research Collaboration Across Tennessee
The funding will also expand collaboration with the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga.
Starting in 2026, researchers at UTC’s Nanoengineering Center will contribute theoretical and simulation expertise to complement UT Knoxville’s experimental materials research.
High-fidelity simulations will help researchers understand the mechanisms responsible for material performance and degradation.
AI-assisted predictive models will also help reduce reliance on trial-and-error experimentation.
The collaboration is intended to generate more information from each experiment while accelerating the development of materials for military applications.
Developing Materials For Extreme Environments
Military equipment frequently operates under extreme temperatures, mechanical stresses, and other challenging conditions.
The university is developing lightweight, stable, and fatigue-tolerant composites that combine the strengths of multiple materials.
These technologies could improve the performance and reliability of military components while supporting more efficient manufacturing.
The renewed ARL sponsorship also provides research opportunities for faculty and students across the university system.
KEY QUOTES:
“As fundamental scientists, we’re trying to understand a material’s chemistry, structure, and performance—but integrating with ARL means we’re also hearing from the folks who will eventually deploy it. That accelerates the translation of new technologies into deployable solutions.”
Katharine Page, Professor Of Materials Science And Engineering And Lead Investigator For DARC’s ARL Research

The post Air Space Intelligence Receives $26 Million Air Force Flyways AI Software Contract appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Air Space Intelligence Receives $26 Million Air Force Flyways AI Software Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:08 AM
Air Space Intelligence Receives $26 Million Air Force Flyways AI Software Contract
Air Space Intelligence Federal has received a $26 million Air Force purchase order for Flyways AI commercial software licenses and platform customization.
The Cambridge, Massachusetts-based small business will provide the cloud-hosted Flyways Artificial Intelligence Platform for use by the 618th Air Operations Center.
Work will be performed at Scott Air Force Base, Illinois, and is expected to continue through September 28, 2031.
The firm-fixed-price purchase order was issued as a sole-source acquisition under contract FA4452-26-P-0019. The award was made on September 28, 2026, although it appeared in the government’s November 9 contract announcement.
The Air Force will obligate $5 million in fiscal 2026 Transportation Working Capital Funds at the time of award. This is the reported initial funded amount and should be distinguished from the full $26 million purchase-order value.
Flyways is an AI-based aviation platform designed to support planning and operational decision-making. For the 618th Air Operations Center, the software will be used and customized within an organization responsible for planning, tasking, and controlling global air mobility missions.
Cloud-hosted software can provide planners with scalable computing, regularly updated capabilities, and centralized access to operational information. AI tools may assist with analyzing routes, constraints, schedules, and changing conditions, although the source announcement does not provide a detailed list of functions.
The 763rd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron at Scott Air Force Base is the contracting activity. The squadron supports enterprise acquisitions connected to Air Mobility Command and related organizations.
Because the procurement was sole-source, the government did not solicit competing proposals for this purchase order. The announcement does not provide the specific statutory justification for that determination.
The five-year performance period gives the Air Force continuing access to software licenses and customization support. Additional funding beyond the initial $5 million may be obligated during performance, subject to requirements and available appropriations.

articles.title: Medical Robotics Startup MedInTech Raises USD 25.7M Series C to Expand AI Robotic Endoscopes Into Surgical Robots
articles.snippet: Medical Robotics Startup MedInTech Raises USD 25.7M Series C to Expand AI Robotic Endoscopes Into Surgical Robots Wowtale
articles.text:
MedInTech , a medical robotics startup, has raised a SeriesC round of USD 25.7 million (33.8 billion won). It plans to use the money to broaden its AI robotic endoscope lineup and move from diagnostic endoscopes into higher-value treatment and surgical applications.
Existing investor Atinum Investment and new investor KB Investment co-led the round. Existing investors Smilegate Investment , SL Investment , ICF (Nextrans) and Wooshin Venture Investment joined with follow-on investments. K2 Investment Partners came in as a new investor. The funds were paid in on the 2nd and 13th, and MedInTech plans to close the Series C round with additional funding within the year.
MedInTech previously raised a Series A of USD 6.1 million (8 billion won) in 2022 and a Series B of USD 15.2 million (20 billion won) in 2024. Including the new round, its cumulative funding comes to about USD 47.3 million (62.2 billion won). Since the Series B, the company has been running clinical validation and commercialization of its AI robotic endoscope and building domestic and overseas distribution. The new round provides the funds for a wider product portfolio and next-generation surgical robot development.
Autonomous steering as the core technology
Founded in 2020, MedInTech develops AI robotic endoscopes that combine robotic precision control and artificial intelligence with gastrointestinal endoscopy, a field that has relied on manual operation by clinicians for decades. Its flagship product, INTION S, uses motor-based precision control. In conventional endoscopes, clinicians steer by pulling wires by hand.
The company says its core strength is extending AI from image analysis to controlling the physical movement of a medical device. Existing medical AI has mostly been used to detect lesions in images or support clinical judgment. MedInTech has built autonomous steering technology that turns what the AI recognizes into endoscope movement. This lowers the operating burden on clinicians and can assist with parts of the procedure, such as steering the scope and tracking lesions.
The robot-drive and precision-control technology developed for diagnostic endoscopes can also be applied to therapeutic endoscopes and surgical robots. MedInTech’s growth strategy is to go beyond competing in the existing endoscope market. It aims to combine AI and robotics that support clinicians’ techniques into a medical physical AI platform covering diagnosis, treatment and surgery.
Clinical results and commercialization
In a clinical trial with 178 adults at Seoul National University Hospital, MedInTech confirmed non-inferiority in key maneuverability measures against conventional mechanical endoscopes. The trial also showed reduced physical fatigue and workload for clinicians. The results were published in the international journal Scientific Reports, and the company has since examined the product’s potential clinical use through multicenter trials.
After launching INTION S in Korea, MedInTech has expanded supply to medical institutions under a distribution agreement with DK Healthcare. It has supplied the product to institutions including the National Fire Service Hospital and Ajou University Hospital, and has recorded initial sales in three overseas markets: Thailand, the Philippines and Mongolia.
